about: The Cosmic Atlas: one record per stage of the journey. The page reads its text, labels, sources and camera framing from here. Ages are years after the Big Bang as [earliest, latest]; null means the stage is not tied to one epoch.

events.title: Primordial energy
events.label: model
events.note: Hot, dense and almost uniform. Space itself is expanding, and tiny fluctuations will seed everything that follows. At 380,000 years the universe turns transparent.

events.title: Structure emerges
events.label: observed
events.era: hundreds of millions of years on
events.note: Gravity pulls dark matter and gas into filaments and nodes. Galaxy surveys map this web; the shape drawn here is procedural, not survey data.

events.title: A young galaxy blazes
events.label: observed
events.era: about 10 billion years ago, when quasars peaked
events.scale: tens of thousands of light-years, jets far beyond
events.note: Inside one node of the web, galaxies collide and gas pours inward. Giant clumps of new stars, tidal tails, and a core outshining everything, firing twin jets.

events.title: The galaxy settles
events.label: observed
events.era: over the next several billion years
events.note: The mergers calm down, the central black hole runs short of fuel and goes quiet, and the gas settles into a rotating spiral. The pattern here is procedural.

events.title: The dark heart
events.label: observed
events.era: at the centre of nearly every large galaxy
events.scale: ours fits inside Mercury's orbit; the largest outsize the solar system
events.note: A supermassive black hole. Telescopes have imaged the ring of light around two of them and tracked stars orbiting ours. This view is procedural.

events.title: A stellar nursery
events.label: observed
events.note: Back out in a spiral arm: a cold cloud of gas and dust, lit by young stars. Red is glowing hydrogen, teal is oxygen. Dense knots are where stars begin.

events.title: A cloud collapses
events.label: observed
events.era: 4.6 billion years ago, for our Sun
events.note: One knot falls in on itself. Spin flattens the infalling gas into a disc, and the newborn star fires narrow jets from its poles.

events.title: A star ignites
events.label: observed
events.note: Fusion begins. Around the star, dust settles into a disc with rings and gaps, like those ALMA imaged around the young star HL Tauri.

events.title: Worlds form
events.label: model
events.era: the next 100 million years or so
events.note: Dust sticks, clumps and collides into planets: small rocky ones close in, giants beyond the frost line where ice survives. Sizes are exaggerated.

events.title: The star sheds its shell
events.label: model
events.era: about 5 billion years from now, for our Sun
events.note: Our Sun will swell into a red giant, swallow its innermost planets and push its outer layers into space. Older Sun-like stars are doing this now.

events.title: The universe looks back
events.label: observed
events.era: about 5 billion years from now; the Helix shows it today
events.note: What our Sun will leave behind. The Helix Nebula, about 650 light-years away, is a real shell like this. The shape is procedural; the eye is our reading.
